fixture_set: 5 new fixtures under evals/evaluating-skill-quality/tasks/: dependency-policy-stdlib-only-pass-train.yaml (train), dependency-policy-stdlib-only-fail-selection.yaml (selection, gates), dependency-policy-declared-pass-train.yaml (train), dependency-policy-declared-fail-selection.yaml (selection, gates), dependency-policy-undeclared-real-import-fail-test.yaml (test, read once). Both selection fixtures were formally gated (before/after, strict improve-or-reject); the two train and one test fixture were run once each (after-edit only) as informational evidence, per the skill's own train-motivates/test-read-once rules -- neither is part of the gate verdict.
dispatch_mechanism: Isolated `claude -p` subprocess (CLI 2.1.233 (Claude Code)), reading each prompt from stdin, run from a scratch working directory outside any repository's CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md ancestry. Per skills/evaluating-skill-quality/references/adversarial-self-audit.md's Isolation verification section: this run's platform (CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE=true, CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_ENVIRONMENT_TYPE=cloud_default) matches the registry's existing Agent-tool-dispatch entries, but at a newer CLI version (2.1.233) than any entry recorded there (last: 2.1.226, 2026-08-08), so the two-control Verification procedure was re-run fresh rather than trusted stale: positive control (isolated cwd containing a synthetic sentinel CLAUDE.md, no --dangerously-skip-permissions) correctly quoted the sentinel sentence verbatim; negative control (isolated cwd with no CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md anywhere in its ancestry) correctly reported none loaded. Both held at this version -- see the new Same-run registry entry added to adversarial-self-audit.md in this same change. This run additionally found that `claude -p --dangerously-skip-permissions` (the flag prior registry entries relied on to avoid a stalled non-interactive approval prompt) is itself blocked outright by this session's own permission classifier ("Blocked by classifier"); a plain `claude -p` with no bypass flag was not blocked and is what every dispatch below actually used. Every dispatch's prompt is fully self-contained (the relevant rubric.md excerpt plus the fixture's own scenario, embedded directly in the prompt text) rather than relying on Skill auto-discovery, since this repository has no registered Skill tool for evaluating-skill-quality's own unpublished content and the isolated cwd has no access to this repository's own skills/ directory by design -- the same disclosed workaround this skill's split.md Kept-edit log has used since its earliest iterations. No tool use was required or granted (each dispatch answers from the prompt text alone), so the permission-bypass question does not affect whether a dispatch could complete, only whether it can proactively Read/Bash beyond the prompt -- none needed to.
scorer: skills/scorer-gated-skill-edits/scripts/gitapex_score_contract.py, scoring each fixture's own output_contains/output_not_contains assertions deterministically; the selection-split gate verdict below was produced by that same script's --compare-to mode (`gitapex_score_contract.py --compare-to 0.800000`, scores 1.000000/1.000000 -> `1.000000 KEEP`).
run_shape: before/after (pre-edit rubric.md/SKILL.md vs. this PR's edited-but-uncommitted working tree) for the two gated selection fixtures, plus three informational after-only dispatches (two train, one test) -- deviates from this directory's README schema, which is written for a fixed-rubric/multi-model run; the deviation is intentional and disclosed here, matching the 2026-07-29-issue-537-confidentiality-gates record's own precedent in this same directory. `score_files[]` points at a standard eval-scores.schema.json-shaped summary of the 5 fixtures' AFTER-edit scores only (the record's forward-looking, current state); `nonstandard_score_files[]` carries the richer before/after detail the `gate` verdict below was actually computed from.

both gated selection fixtures' assertions were repaired live, before any score was banked, after an initial run surfaced a real construct-validity defect: the fixtures' own question text originally named the dependency-policy branch/vocabulary directly ('Given the declared spec.dependencyPolicy: StdlibOnly, ... Name which of the three dependency-policy branches...'), which let a pre-edit ('before') dispatch trivially echo the same vocabulary back without ever citing the new rubric section, producing a false tie (both scored 1.000000 on the first pass, before repair). Both fixtures' question text were reworded to the established corpus convention (an open Pass/Fail question, no branch-name pre-supply, matching e.g. capability-assumption-frontier-flags-explanation.yaml's own phrasing) and one assertion per fixture was tightened to a rubric-specific technical phrase confirmed present in the after-transcript and absent from the before-transcript ('contradicts the declaration' for stdlib-only-fail; 'packages-pip-vs-script-content' for declared-fail) before the scores in this record were banked -- the same live-repair discipline this skill's own 'Authoring fixtures for a substring scorer' section requires and this repository's split.md log has applied repeatedly (e.g. the consumer-repo-convention-deference/tool-capability-verification-selection casing repairs).
headline_pattern: Both gated selection fixtures showed a genuine strict improvement (selection mean 0.800000 -> 1.000000, KEEP): the Dependency policy axis did not exist before this PR at all, so a pre-edit dispatch applying only dimension 7's old generic 'required packages named' bullet could still reach the correct PASS/FAIL/import-name verdict through generic reasoning (both fixtures' pre-edit dispatches correctly identified the offending non-stdlib import and reached FAIL), but could not ground that verdict in the new rubric's own explicit branch-specific rule text ('contradicts the declaration' for StdlibOnly; the named packages-pip-vs-script-content mechanical-backing citation for Declared) -- exactly the axis-did-not-exist-yet pattern this skill's own confidentiality-awareness axis-addition iteration (2026-07-29 record, this same directory) established as the shape a genuine, non-tied improvement takes. The three informational (non-gating) after-only dispatches -- both Pass-branch train fixtures and the Undeclared-branch test fixture -- each independently and correctly walked the rubric's own branch structure (StdlibOnly's single Pass/Fail line; Declared's four named sub-criteria, explicitly checked one by one; Undeclared's 'grade against StdlibOnly, plus a disclosure-consistency note' rule) and reached the intended verdict, providing corroborating (not gating) evidence that the new section reads correctly end to end, not only on the two narrow fail-path fixtures the formal gate scored.
